topic: first irrigation timing weeks after sowing light irrigation pre-sowing irrigation rauni
text: PAU advises a relatively light first irrigation about 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown wheat and about 4 weeks after sowing for later-sown wheat. It suggests bringing the first irrigation forward on light soils and delaying it by a week on heavy paddy soils. A heavy pre-sowing irrigation of about 10 cm is recommended before sowing, except when wheat follows rice.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat irrigation (p. 16)

topic: irrigation schedule second third fourth irrigation interval weeks rain end of March
text: PAU puts the first irrigation about 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown wheat and about 4 weeks after sowing for later-sown wheat. For wheat sown on sandy loam or heavier soils, PAU then gives the later intervals in weeks after the previous irrigation. Sown up to 21 November: second irrigation 5 to 6 weeks, third 5 to 6 weeks, fourth 4 weeks. Sown 22 November to 20 December: 5 to 6, 3 to 4 and 2 weeks. Sown 21 December to 15 January: 4, 3 and 2 weeks. These irrigations are about 7.5 cm each and the intervals can shift by 2 to 3 days either side. Each cm of rain lengthens the next interval by about 5 days until the end of January and by 2 days after that. Timely-sown wheat is irrigated up to the end of March depending on rain, and wheat sown after 5 December up to 10 April. Irrigation should be avoided on windy days to reduce lodging.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat irrigation (p. 16)

topic: urea nitrogen fertilizer top dressing first second irrigation split dose phosphorus DAP at sowing
text: PAU recommends drilling all the phosphorus at sowing (55 kg DAP per acre on medium-fertility soil) and no urea at sowing when DAP is used. Urea is broadcast in two doses of 45 kg per acre before the first and second irrigations for timely-sown wheat, and 35 kg each for wheat sown after mid-December. If rain delays the second irrigation, the urea is applied about 55 days after sowing. If water is standing near the second irrigation, urea is not broadcast; two sprays of 7.5% urea solution (15 kg urea in 200 litres of water per acre) are given at 42 and 54 days after sowing.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat fertilizer application (pp. 9-10)

topic: fertilizer dose per acre without soil test medium fertility nitrogen phosphorus potash kallar
text: Fertilizer should follow a soil test. Without one, PAU gives for medium-fertility soil 50 kg nitrogen and 25 kg phosphorus (P2O5) per acre, which works out to about 90 kg urea plus 55 kg DAP. Potash (20 kg muriate of potash per acre) is applied only to soils testing low in potassium. Crops on kallar soil get 25% more nitrogen, and crops sown after mid-December get 25% less.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat fertilizer application (pp. 9-10)

topic: sowing time date November optimum late sowing yield loss variety
text: The optimum sowing time for wheat in Punjab is the first fortnight of November. Long-duration varieties can be sown from the fourth week of October, and timely-sown varieties are sown from the fourth week of October to the fourth week of November. A delay of one week from the optimum time cuts yield by about 150 kg per acre. Late-sown crops use late-sown varieties such as PBW 771 and PBW 752.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat time of sowing (p. 5)

topic: sowing depth cm seed rate row spacing drill happy seeder
text: With a seed-cum-fertilizer drill PAU recommends sowing wheat at 4 to 6 cm depth with rows 15 to 20 cm apart (15 cm if late sown). In bi-directional sowing the seed goes in slightly shallower, at 4 cm in rows 20 cm apart. With a Happy Seeder the sowing depth is 1.5 to 2 inches. Seed rate is 40 kg per acre for most varieties and 45 kg for PBW 869 and Unnat PBW 550, with 5 kg more per acre when sowing with a Happy Seeder.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat sowing method and seed rate (pp. 5-8)

topic: weed control weeding herbicide hand hoeing gulli danda Phalaris minor timing broadleaf
text: PAU's first option is two hand hoeings, one before and one after the first irrigation. For herbicides, pre-emergence sprays go on within 2 days of sowing. Post-emergence sprays for grass weeds such as gulli danda go on either when the crop is about 20 days old and the weeds have 2 to 3 leaves (2 to 3 days before the first irrigation) or 30 to 35 days after sowing. Broadleaf weed sprays fall between 25 and 45 days after sowing (45 to 55 days for December sowings). The right product depends on the weed, soil texture and the next crop, so it should be chosen from the package or with the KVK. Irrigation after spraying should be light, and the herbicide group should be changed every year.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat weed control (pp. 12-16)

topic: yellow rust stripe rust disease symptoms yellow powdery stripes monitoring December
text: Yellow rust shows as yellow powdery pustules forming stripes on the leaves. PAU advises monitoring wheat from the second week of December onward, especially after irrigation or rain, treating the first patches early and spraying only around the infected area. Nights of 7 to 13 degrees C with 85 to 100% humidity and days of 15 to 24 degrees C favour it, and frequent rain with wind in February and March makes it worse. Resistant varieties are advised, and October sowing is discouraged in disease-prone sub-mountainous areas. Fungicide options are listed in the package and should be confirmed with the KVK.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat diseases (pp. 19-20)

topic: harvest maturity days ripe shattering threshing storage moisture grain
text: PAU advises harvesting and threshing wheat as soon as it is fully ripe, because late harvest causes heavy grain loss from shattering. Timely-sown varieties in its list mature in roughly 145 to 158 days. Grain with more than 10% moisture should be dried before storage to avoid mould and heat damage.
source_title: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26: wheat harvesting and storage (p. 17)
